item.title: Reporters’ Social Media Challenge Lands With a Thud
item.description: They find posting feels like a performance rather than real communication

item.title: China’s Tame Inflation Is Negative for Domestic Outlook But Win for World
item.description: China’s inflation momentum appeared to stall in June. That’s both good and bad news for the world.

item.title: Senator Wyden Says Trump Tariffs Are ‘Ill-Designed’ to Combat Forced Labor Globally
item.description: Top Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee takes aim at Trump’s latest tariffs proposal

item.title: Fuel Prices Show Inflation Is Still a Risk for Markets
item.description: While oil prices have fallen, the cost of refined products like gasoline and diesel are proving to be much stickier.

item.title: TCS Meets Estimate After Deal Momentum Boosts Recovery
item.description: Tata Consultancy Services Ltd. reported quarterly earnings that met analysts’ estimates after a string of cost-cutting efforts and data center deals helped Asia’s largest outsourcer weather a slump in the sector.

item.title: India’s Wartime Buying Spree Leaves Behind a Cooking Gas Surplus
item.description: India’s frenzied efforts to counter disruptions in cooking gas supplies over the past months, while cargoes remained trapped in the Persian Gulf, has left state-run fuel retailers with the opposite problem — more than they can sell.

item.title: Russian Rail Giant Wants Business to Bear More War Economy Pain
item.description: Russia’s largest employer is trying to address mounting financial pressures with new measures that some businesses worry will come at their expense, underscoring the growing strains on the economy as President Vladimir Putin’s war in Ukraine drags on.

item.title: Labor Shortages Are Putting a Bug in the Data Center Build
item.description: Contractors like Sterling Infrastructure and Comfort Systems USA have more work than they have skilled labor for.

item.title: Nigerian Stocks Vault Past Korea’s Kospi to Claim World’s Top Returns
item.description: Nigerian equities have overtaken South Korea’s to hand investors the highest dollar-based returns this year, as souring sentiment on artificial-intelligence stocks pushes the Asian nation’s world-beating rally into bear territory.

item.title: Starbucks Taps AI to Reduce Reliance on Microsoft, IBM Software
item.description: Starbucks Corp. is developing in-house tools with the help of artificial intelligence that could replace some software applications it now buys from companies such as Microsoft Corp. and International Business Machines Corp.

item.title: Serbia Holds Rates as Election Welfare Plans Signal Price Risks
item.description: Serbia kept borrowing costs unchanged for a record 22nd month as a government plan for cash handouts before this year’s general election may add to inflation pressures.

item.title: Warsh to Get Some Inflation Relief From Upcoming PCE Makeover
item.description: A coming revamp of the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge could be just enough to tip the scales against interest-rate increases this year, even if it doesn’t dramatically alter the overall picture on prices.

item.title: Erste Shares to Rally 30% on Poland Growth, Goldman Sachs Says
item.description: Erste Group Bank AG shares are set to rally 30%, driven by growth from the lender’s expansion in Poland, according to Goldman Sachs Group Inc.

item.title: Barclays Readies $875 Million Debt Sale for Buyout of Senior Plc
item.description: Barclays Plc is preparing to sell about $875 million of debt financing used to fund a takeover of UK aerospace supplier Senior Plc.

item.title: Defense Valuations Yet to Peak as Orders Surge, BNP Banker Says
item.description: European defense sector valuations still have plenty of upside, with government pledges to boost military spending now translating into orders, according to a top banker at BNP Paribas SA.

item.title: Turkey’s Vestel Hires Advisers for Dollar Bond Restructuring
item.description: Turkey’s Vestel Elektronik has hired advisers Houlihan Lokey for restructuring talks with bondholders, at the same time as the struggling electronics manufacturer renegotiates loans with local banks.

item.title: Fujimori Legacy Shows Limits of Trump’s Push Against China in Peru
item.description: Alberto Fujimori’s first trip to Beijing 35 years ago helped turn Peru toward China, anticipating a broader Latin American realignment that Washington is still struggling to reverse.

item.title: BlackRock’s Jewell Sees AI Capex Stable for Two to Three Years
item.description: Commitments for AI spending should sustain the investment theme around the technology for two to three years, even as tech giants gradually turn cash-flow negative and start raising debt to fund their buildouts, according to BlackRock Inc.’s Helen Jewell.

item.title: Hugo Boss Board Rejects Frasers Bid as Not Reflecting Potential
item.description: Hugo Boss AG recommended shareholders reject Frasers Group Plc’s takeover offer, saying the bid fails to capture the German fashion company’s long-term value.

item.title: UK’s Capita Sinks on Profit Hit From Pension Contract Failures
item.description: Capita Plc tumbled after it said profit and cash flow will be hit by its failure to deliver on a contract to manage Britain’s civil service pension plan.

item.title: Thailand and Malaysia Reach Deal to End Seafood Trade Spat
item.description: Thailand and Malaysia have resolved a seafood trade dispute, paving the way for fishery trade between the two countries to return to normal soon, their leaders said.

item.title: France Plans €2 Billion to Cut Fertilizer Imports Dependence
item.description: France will invest €2 billion ($2.3 billion) to cut dependence on fertilizer imports in an effort to shield farmers from future supply disruptions.

item.title: Market Warns UK’s Plan for Long-Dated Debt Needs a Rethink
item.description: Investors say that another bout of political uncertainty will force the UK to scale back planned sales of long-dated debt.

item.title: German Exports Unexpectedly Increase as US Sales Rebound
item.description: German exports unexpectedly rose in May, extending their run of growth to a fourth straight month thanks to a sharp rebound in shipments to the US.

item.title: Wall Street Banks Miss Multibillion-Dollar AI Deals in Hong Kong
item.description: Wall Street banks were largely absent from a $5.8 billion fundraising spree by Chinese artificial intelligence stars in Hong Kong this week.

item.title: US, Iran Trade Attacks for Second Day, Testing Fragile Ceasefire
item.description: The US military struck Iran for a second day and Tehran retaliated against American allies in the Persian Gulf, raising fears that the tit-for-tat attacks may derail talks on a permanent peace deal.

item.title: European Gas Edges Lower as Traders Assess Middle East Flare-Up
item.description: European natural gas prices edged lower as traders evaluate the region’s supply picture after fresh hostilities between the US and Iran.

item.title: Taiwan Dollar Hits 14-Month Low on Greenback Gains, Dividends
item.description: The Taiwan dollar fell to its weakest level since April 2025, erasing gains from last year’s historic rally as dollar strength and record dividend payouts weighed on sentiment.

item.title: Malaysia Holds Rates on Modest Inflation, Resilient Growth
item.description: Malaysia kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged for a sixth straight meeting, saying the level is appropriate as price pressures remain contained despite the Middle East conflict.
